reference: No matching GNU NetIDS CLI is available to this harness; Suricata is not treated as a GNU oracle. Contract expectations come from the netids source comments and registered help contract. Classic PCAP records are independently encoded with Python struct layouts matching the published PCAP little-endian header, Ethernet II, IPv4 and UDP field layouts; packet timestamps, IPs, ports and payload bytes are fixed inputs. Expected event lines are independently assembled from those fixed packet fields and the documented schema-level event fields, not captured from the candidate.
coverage: Bash type/help/version metadata (metadata only; not counted as operation coverage).
Compile accepted rule count, CIDR/port-range syntax, bidirectional ip rule, and explicit PCRE opt-in.
Fail-closed compile rejection of an unsupported flowbits directive and PCRE when opt-in is absent.
Offline Ethernet IPv4/UDP alert matching, destination-port/CIDR filtering, nocase content, and -o file output readback.
Offline raw IPv4 decoding, binary hex content decoding, and AND semantics across content clauses.
Malformed PCAP failure and offline drop event under explicit dry-run only.
exclusions: No GNU-compatible NetIDS CLI oracle is present; netids behavior cases are documented contracts, not GNU parity.
Live interface capture, active fw/firewall mutation, and real network interactions are deferred.
The suite does not cover IPv6, complete Suricata compatibility, or PCRE packet-match semantics.
No other bash-os loadable is tested.
A generic Bash-only redirection check is excluded because it never invokes netids and cannot establish loadable operation parity.

cases.purpose: Check that Bash registers netids as a builtin, exposes its help text, and returns the documented version banner; this is metadata coverage only.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help netids)
[[ -n $help_text ]]
type -t netids
printf '%s\n' 'help-present'
netids --version
cases.stdout:
builtin
help-present
netids (bash-os AUDIT-6.4 A5 A6) NetIDS; Suricata subset, offline -r + live -i, pcre opt-in, blocking opt-in

cases.purpose: Compile two documented subset rules, including a TCP port range, CIDR, bidirectional ip rule, and PCRE enabled explicitly; expected count follows the documented compile contract.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '# fixture rules' 'alert tcp 192.0.2.0/24 1024:65535 -> 198.51.100.5 443 (msg:"tls client"; pcre:"/ClientHello/i"; sid:101; rev:2; classtype:policy-violation;)' 'pass ip any any <> any any (msg:"baseline"; sid:102;)' > rules
netids compile -S rules --enable-pcre

cases.purpose: Verify the documented fail-closed rule-subset behavior for flowbits; unsupported directives reject the whole rule file with status 2.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'alert udp any any -> any any (msg:"fixture"; flowbits:set,seen; sid:1;)' > rules
netids compile -S rules

cases.purpose: Verify the documented default that pcre rules are rejected unless --enable-pcre or its environment opt-in is supplied.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'alert tcp any any -> any any (msg:"fixture"; pcre:"/hello/i"; sid:21;)' > rules
netids compile -S rules

cases.purpose: Scan an independently encoded little-endian classic PCAP Ethernet/IPv4/UDP frame; verify CIDR, destination port, nocase content, deterministic alert fields, and -o file output via Bash readback.
cases.script:
pcap_bytes='\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1\x02\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\xf1\x53\x65\x40\xe2\x01\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x08\x00\x45\x00\x00\x21\x00\x01\x00\x00\x40\x11\x00\x00\xc0\x00\x02\x01\xc6\x33\x64\x02\x30\x39\x00\x35\x00\x0d\x00\x00\x48\x45\x4c\x4c\x4f'
printf '%b' "$pcap_bytes" > traffic.pcap
printf '%s\n' 'alert udp 192.0.2.0/24 any -> 198.51.100.2 53 (msg:"dns hello"; content:"hello"; nocase; sid:7; rev:1; classtype:attempted-admin;)' > rules
netids scan -r traffic.pcap -S rules -o events
IFS= read -r event < events
printf '%s\n' "$event"

cases.purpose: Check case-sensitive content matching and destination-port filtering: the packet payload is uppercase HELLO, so neither the lowercase-only rule nor the rule for port 54 alerts.
cases.script:
pcap_bytes='\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1\x02\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\xf1\x53\x65\x40\xe2\x01\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x08\x00\x45\x00\x00\x21\x00\x01\x00\x00\x40\x11\x00\x00\xc0\x00\x02\x01\xc6\x33\x64\x02\x30\x39\x00\x35\x00\x0d\x00\x00\x48\x45\x4c\x4c\x4f'
printf '%b' "$pcap_bytes" > traffic.pcap
printf '%s\n' 'alert udp any any -> any 53 (msg:"wrong case"; content:"hello"; sid:31;)' 'alert udp any any -> any 54 (msg:"wrong port"; content:"HELLO"; sid:32;)' > rules
netids scan -r traffic.pcap -S rules

cases.purpose: Scan an independently encoded raw-IPv4 PCAP record and verify raw linktype decoding plus AND semantics across literal and hex content clauses containing binary bytes.
cases.script:
pcap_bytes='\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1\x02\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x00\x00\x65\x00\x00\x00\x01\xf1\x53\x65\xf1\xfb\x09\x00\x21\x00\x00\x00\x21\x00\x00\x00\x45\x00\x00\x21\x00\x01\x00\x00\x40\x11\x00\x00\xcb\x00\x71\x07\xcb\x00\x71\x09\x9c\x40\x14\xe9\x00\x0d\x00\x00\x41\x42\x01\x02\x21'
printf '%b' "$pcap_bytes" > traffic.pcap
printf '%s\n' 'alert udp any any -> any 5353 (msg:"raw bytes"; content:"AB"; content:"|01 02|"; content:"!"; sid:9; rev:2;)' > rules
netids scan -r traffic.pcap -S rules

cases.purpose: Verify a malformed offline capture is rejected with a failing status and diagnostic instead of being treated as an empty successful scan.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'alert udp any any -> any any (msg:"fixture"; sid:1;)' > rules
printf '%s' 'bad' > traffic.pcap
netids scan -r traffic.pcap -S rules

cases.purpose: Exercise offline drop-rule matching only with both --enable-blocking and --dry-run; assert the documented block event and dry_run=true without invoking fw or changing firewall state.
cases.script:
pcap_bytes='\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1\x02\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\xf1\x53\x65\x40\xe2\x01\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x2f\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x08\x00\x45\x00\x00\x21\x00\x01\x00\x00\x40\x11\x00\x00\xc0\x00\x02\x01\xc6\x33\x64\x02\x30\x39\x00\x35\x00\x0d\x00\x00\x48\x45\x4c\x4c\x4f'
printf '%b' "$pcap_bytes" > traffic.pcap
printf '%s\n' 'drop udp any any -> any 53 (msg:"fixture block"; content:"HELLO"; sid:44; rev:3;)' > rules
netids scan -r traffic.pcap -S rules --enable-blocking --dry-run

cases.purpose: Qualify the -i interface path with a bounded one-packet capture.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated isolated veth pair, an independently verified packet injector on the peer, and a known interface name. This harness intentionally has no real network target or live-capture fixture.

cases.purpose: Verify non-dry-run drop/reject behavior and the exact fw deny request.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM/network namespace and a reviewed mock fw executable that records argv and cannot reach host firewall state. The active path is deliberately not invoked; the current candidate fixture PATH is empty and no firewall shim is supplied.
